newsitem.title: USA: Sperling says rates could rise without budget pact.
newsitem.headline: Sperling says rates could rise without budget pact.

text.p: White House Economic Adviser Gene Sperling on Thursday said there is a risk that interest rates could begin to rise and the economy would be less robust if negotiators fail to reach a balanced budget agreement this year.
Speaking to a business group, Sperling said there is an expectation that an agreement will be arrived at and if it is not achieved, there could be adverse economic ramifications.
"I think we'll see a risk that long term interest rates will start to rise and we will see a less robust economy because of the increase in long-term interest rates," he said.
He told the group that the administration was flexible in its position on the budget and he was cautiously optimitic that agreement would be achieved.
Sperling, asked about the Consumer Price Index bias, said it was the view of the administration economic team that there was some overstatement although it was very difficult to say how large it was.
"We are committed to dealing with this," he said, but "things need to be done in a way that they have the right amount of support."
